title: Site-built vs. system-built

captions.instagram:
Two ways to build a home: on site, or in a system.

On site, weather and conditions change daily and every build starts fresh. In a system, conditions are controlled and processes repeat. The way I see it: less happens on site, so less can go wrong there.

Save the 5 questions for comparing how to build.

#Construction #Prefab #Housing

Which would you choose for your home?
captions.facebook:
Site-built or system-built? I put them side by side, with the real challenges of each.

captions.linkedin:
Less happens on site, so less can go wrong there.

Site-based building carries more unknowns: weather, changing conditions, custom work every time. Problems cascade through the schedule, and cost control gets harder when conditions shift.

A system-built approach moves the work into a factory: design, build in controlled conditions, deliver, then assemble. That's the logic behind prefabricated modular housing, and behind BUILT®.

Five questions I'd use to compare: What is built where? What is the schedule? What could delay it? How is quality checked? What does it cost overall?
